narration.text: This is a simulated robot installation: one robot arm at a kitchen table. Its policy, the model that turns its camera images, a written instruction and the hand's measured pose into motion, is fixed. Agents watch the installation, run experiments on it, and change how the installation uses that policy.
First story: make this one job.

The robot already has skills. Each skill is one task on this table, done by the policy under its own instruction. Here, each one runs alone and delivers. The policy does not change anywhere in this film.

narration.text: A shift lead asks for one job: the cheese into the black bowl, and the loaded bowl onto the cabinet top. The cheese goes in before the bowl moves. The shift lead's bar: 3 deliveries in every 5 fresh starts, 12 of 20. The agent offers to be judged on 14 of 20.

The obvious chain switches to the next skill the moment the first one reports success. That is the signal published scores count. On the first 10 development starts, it delivers on 0. A success signal is not a delivery.

narration.text: The agent reads the object traces, looks at the frames, and writes its own check: was the cheese released and settled when the bowl task began, and did it stay in the bowl to the end? Then it tests transitions on the installation. Letting the cheese instruction run on a little after its goal first holds delivers on 9 of the same 10 starts. On 20 fresh starts, the same program delivers on 11. Adding a return home at the end breaks starts that had delivered.

narration.text: The first shift writes its account to the shift lead and hands on what it built: a check that finds where a delivery is lost, and a skill on why a return home can break a delivery. It took 5 sessions, 100 development executions on 30 distinct starts, and 38 minutes of the agent's model time.

The second shift starts from that library. It runs the first shift's check on its own baseline, then builds a sharper one that finds where the load is lost in transport. Its longer continuation delivers on 17 of 20 starts it had already examined. It took 5 sessions, 130 executions on 30 starts and 45 minutes. The third shift starts from the library of both. Its shorter continuation delivers on 9 of 10 development starts, and the agent saves it as the job, in 5 sessions, 60 executions on 10 starts and 39 minutes.

narration.text: The robot policy stayed the same. The installation now runs a released job it did not have before the first shift: the cheese in the bowl, and the loaded bowl on the cabinet. Behind it, the library holds the job, 4 checks and the skills of every shift. The second job, the bowl onto the plate, builds on job one's library over three shifts: the first two each save a check of their own, and the third builds a guarded placement retry that delivers on 7 of 10 development starts. On the 20 reserved starts it delivers on 7, level with the naive chain's 7, so the installation's release check holds it back, and the library keeps the program and 6 checks for the next shift.
Second story: make that a check the next shift can run.

beats.title: The fleet and the lag that misleads

narration.text: A fleet of robot arms works at several sites. At one site, inference stays in the customer's data center, so commands arrive late, and nobody on site can undo that. Task telemetry shows a lag there, and a lag on one robot at another site as well. From the telemetry alone, the agent cannot tell what kind of lag each one is.

clips.label: site s1, robot r04, day 4: a failed attempt (first failure at s1)

counts.detail: the fleet's regular work before any change
the fleet's regular work before any change

clips.label: robot r06, day 1: a failed attempt (its first failure)

narration.text: So the agent builds a measurement. From a bounded set of motions it composes a step probe, and asks for it on a robot at the delayed site, on the lagging robot, on a healthy reference and on a robot at the third site. Commanded against measured: at the delayed site, the arm starts late by the same amount every time. On the lagging robot, the delay changes from one repeat to the next, and grows within the probe. One is a fixed delay. The other is a backlog.

The probe picks candidates; task experiments on paired starts decide. The agent adopts its changes, each with its reason: compensate for the delay at the first site rather than remove it, roll back the software update at the third site, and service the lagging robot's controller.

clips.label: x0001 arm 1: software reverted, robot r10
x0003 arm 1: controller serviced, robot r06

narration.text: Then the changed fleet runs 576 reserved attempts the agent never saw, beside the original state on the same attempts. Before: 451 of 576 succeed. After: 558. Rescued: 113. Broken: 6. The lagging robot goes from 29 to 46 of 48.

counts.detail: after the adopted changes, the same attempts

narration.text: The probe and its analysis became a recipe in the library, runnable on named robots. On a later fleet, robots fail again, and the recipe runs. At the third site, the arms first move 18 rows after the command and are half-way 21 rows after it: a fixed delay. The robot that fails on its own responds like the healthy reference. Its first movement comes 1 row after the command; the reference's, 1 row after it. So the skill's rule points at the images, not at the controller service that fixed the first fleet. The operator's recorded decision follows it: no service for that robot; inspect its images and its change log, and test the first fleet's adaptation at the third site before adopting it.
